result.name: Hack On Hills 8.0
result.desc:
⚡ Hack on Hills 8.0

The Age of Autonomous Agents

Welcome to Hack on Hills 8.0, the flagship 48-hour hackathon hosted by the App Team, NIT Hamirpur.

Over the years, Hack on Hills has grown into one of North India's largest student-run hackathons, bringing together thousands of developers, designers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts from across the country.

This edition explores a defining shift in technology: the rise of autonomous agents.

As AI systems evolve from tools that generate content to systems that can reason, plan, and execute tasks, we stand at the beginning of a new computing paradigm. Hack on Hills 8.0 invites participants to build products, platforms, and experiences that leverage this transformation to solve real-world problems.

Whether you're building intelligent agents, decentralized applications, sustainable technology solutions, or entirely new ideas, this is your opportunity to turn ambitious concepts into working products.

---

💡 Tracks

🤖 AI & Autonomous Agents

Build systems capable of reasoning, planning, decision-making, and autonomous execution.

⛓️ Blockchain & Web3

Develop decentralized applications, protocols, and infrastructure for the next generation of the internet.

🌱 Sustainability & Social Impact

Create technology solutions addressing environmental, social, and community challenges.

🚀 Open Innovation

Explore bold ideas beyond predefined categories and build solutions that create meaningful impact.

---

⚙️ Format & Eligibility

Team Size: 2-4 Members

Shortlisting: Based on participant profiles and application review

Finals: 48-hour in-person hackathon at NIT Hamirpur

Participants will collaborate, prototype, and present their projects before a panel of industry experts, mentors, and judges.

---

🏆 Prizes & Sponsor Tracks

Hack on Hills 8.0 features a prize pool, sponsor challenges, and ecosystem bounties designed to recognize outstanding innovation across multiple domains.

Prize details and partner tracks will be announced soon.

---

🔥 Why Hack on Hills?

- 48 hours of building, learning, and collaboration
- Mentorship from industry professionals and developer communities
- Networking opportunities with talented builders from across the country
- Exciting sponsor tracks, workshops, and challenges
- A platform to transform ideas into impactful solutions

With over 1,500+ registrations across previous editions, Hack on Hills continues to foster a community of builders who are passionate about technology, innovation, and problem-solving.

---

📍 Venue: NIT Hamirpur

📅 Dates: [Dates to be announced]

Build for the Age of Autonomous Agents.

Join us for 48 hours of innovation, collaboration, and creation at Hack on Hills 8.0.

result.name: Arkiv: Global Tour Stop 🌍
result.tagline: A special edition on the road to Devcon 8 Mumbai. Ten days to build on Arkiv, the Web3 database.
result.desc:
Build on [Arkiv](https://arkiv.network), the Web3 database, around one theme: **CROPS**, the Ethereum Foundation's mandate that Ethereum stay **c**ensorship resistant, **o**pen source, **p**rivate and **s**ecure.

Ten days, fully online, open to builders everywhere. The challenge opens live at Network School Astana during the Network State Conference on **9 October** and closes on **18 October**. Five winners get a Devcon 8 ticket on top of their prize.

Build anything useful and usable for the ecosystem: a dApp, a library, an SDK, a devtool, a CLI, an indexer, a dataset, an agent, a browser extension or more. Four CROPS tracks are open to everyone, and the Best Indian Use Case track rewards a real-world application that people in India can use.

## Prizes

- **Best Indian Use Case:** Devcon 8 ticket + **$2,000 USDC**. A real-world application built on Arkiv that people in India can use. It does not need to follow a CROPS pillar. Your team needs at least one member of Indian nationality.
- **Censorship Resistance (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**
- **Open Source (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**
- **Privacy (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**
- **Security (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**

### Prize conditions

- **One prize per team.** You can enter more than one track, but your team wins at most one prize. If you win Best Indian Use Case, you cannot also win a Global prize. If you win one Global prize, you cannot win another.
- **Attending Devcon is not required to win.**
- **One Devcon ticket per winning team.** Travel, visa and accommodation are the winner's cost.
- Winners accept their prize within 48 hours and complete KYC. Prizes are paid within 14 days after KYC.

## Dates

All times are London time (BST, UTC+1).

- **7 October:** registration opens
- **9 October, 12:00:** opening, live at Network School Astana
- **18 October, 23:59 (22:59 UTC):** submissions close
- **19 to 22 October:** judging. Keep your deployment up.
- **23 October:** winners announced
- **25 October:** deadline for winners to accept their prize
- **3 to 6 November:** Devcon 8, Mumbai

## How it is judged

Pick **one or more tracks** when you submit: the four CROPS pillars and Best Indian Use Case. All projects are scored on four criteria, 25 points each. The first one depends on the track and is scored for each track you enter:

- **Why this pillar?** (CROPS tracks) Who is harmed today if this data is censored, shut down, leaked or forged?
- **Why India?** (Best Indian Use Case) Who in India uses it, and what real problem does it solve for them?
- **Why Arkiv?** What would break on Postgres, IPFS, a subgraph or your own API, and what did you keep off Arkiv on purpose?
- **How you use Arkiv:** how and why you use each Arkiv feature. Not how many you use.
- **Friction report:** specific, reproducible feedback on building with Arkiv.

Before scoring, every project must pass the gates: a public deployment judges can open without asking for access (libraries, CLIs and datasets too), reproducible steps, a public MIT repo, `/arkiv/schema.md`, `/arkiv/friction.md`, the wallet addresses that create your Arkiv entities on Tiramisu, a demo video of 3 minutes or less, every required question on the submission form answered, and work built between 9 and 18 October. Disclose any pre-existing work with its baseline commit SHA. A project needs at least 50/100 to win.

**Disqualified:** plagiarised work; no meaningful Arkiv use (SDK installed but never queried, or a conventional database app with Arkiv branding); private keys, secrets or real personal data stored in Arkiv, in plaintext or hashed (use synthetic data); malicious code; no working app; late entries. At the deadline we record your repo's commit SHA and judge that commit. Rewriting history after the deadline disqualifies the entry. Keep your deployment up until 23 October.

## Build on Tiramisu

- **Network:** Tiramisu testnet, chain ID `7738577`
- **HTTP RPC:** `https://rpc.tiramisu.db-chain.testnet.arkiv.network`
- **WebSocket RPC:** `wss://rpc.tiramisu.db-chain.testnet.arkiv.network`
- **Explorer:** [tiramisu.explorer.arkiv.network](https://tiramisu.explorer.arkiv.network)
- **SDK:** [`@arkiv-network/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@arkiv-network/sdk) 0.8.x
- **Docs:** [docs.arkiv.network](https://docs.arkiv.network/networks/tiramisu/)
- **Arkiv Hub** [hub.arkiv.network/](https://hub.arkiv.network/)

## Rules

The full rules, rubric and submission checklist live in [Arkiv-Network/global-tour-stop-pre-devcon](https://github.com/Arkiv-Network/global-tour-stop-pre-devcon). That repo is the only canonical source: if anything here differs, the repo applies.

Questions: [Arkiv Discord](https://discord.gg/arkiv).

result.name: TUM Blockchain & AI Hackathon
result.tagline: The hackathon where Blockchain and AI meet
result.desc:
## The Theme: Agentic Payments

AI agents are starting to act on their own: booking, negotiating, paying. The payment rails for that don't fully exist yet. This hackathon is about building the infrastructure and applications that let autonomous agents transact safely and instantly on-chain.

## Format

- 30-hour build sprint
- Teams of 1 to 5
- ~200 builders on site
- Mentor office hours throughout the build
- Kickoff briefing, overnight build, live demos and judging

## Prizes

- **BSV Blockchain Track:** €4,000 prize pool
- More sponsor tracks to be announced

## Details

- **Dates:** 30–31 October 2026
- **Venue:** House of Communication, Munich

## Why Build With Us

TUM Blockchain Club has brought together 3,000+ builders, researchers and founders over the last four years, running Europe's largest student-led Web3 event. This year the hackathon sits inside TBC26: three days, two venues, one community, with the main conference and Bundesblock's Digital Assets Day running alongside.
